hero.headline: US proposes rule allowing government to cancel research grants at any time
hero.body:
The US government has proposed new funding rules that would allow officials to terminate research grants at any time, according to a policy draft. The changes would also make peer review optional for grant decisions and introduce screening by political staff to identify forbidden research topics.

The proposed rules represent a substantial shift in how federal research funding operates. Under current practice, grants undergo peer review by independent scientists who evaluate proposals based on scientific merit. The new framework would give political appointees authority to screen applications before approval.

The policy would also eliminate the requirement for peer review in the grant approval process. Peer review has traditionally served as a cornerstone of scientific funding, with researchers in relevant fields assessing the quality and potential impact of proposed studies.

Under the proposed system, political staff would review grant applications to determine whether they address topics the government has designated as forbidden. The draft does not specify which topics would fall under this classification.

The termination provision would give officials discretion to cancel grants after they have been awarded and research has begun. Current grant agreements typically include specific conditions under which funding can be withdrawn, often related to compliance failures or misconduct.

Researchers rely on federal grants to fund laboratories, pay staff, and conduct studies across fields including medicine, climate science, physics, and engineering. Multi-year grants allow scientists to plan long-term projects and maintain research teams.

The proposal comes as the administration examines federal spending across agencies. Research institutions and universities receive billions in federal grants annually to support both basic science and applied research projects.

The changes would affect grants distributed by federal agencies including the National Institutes of Health, the National Science Foundation, and the Department of Energy. These agencies currently award funding through competitive processes that emphasize scientific merit and potential societal benefit.

The proposed rules are subject to a public comment period before any final decision on implementation.

cards.headline: Russian drone strike injures civilians in Romania, first attack on NATO territory
cards.body:
A Russian drone struck an apartment building in Galati, Romania on Friday, injuring two people in the first such attack on a NATO member state, according to Romanian and alliance officials. The incident represents a significant escalation in the spillover from Russia's war in Ukraine.

The drone hit a residential building in Galati, located on the Danube River west of Romania's borders with Moldova and Ukraine. The impact sparked a fire and forced the evacuation of several residents. Romanian military scrambled two F-16 fighter jets and a helicopter authorized to engage targets in response.

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte responded swiftly to the incident. "Russia's reckless behaviour is a danger to us all," Rutte wrote on social media after speaking with Romanian President Nicuşor Dan. "I affirmed that Nato stands ready to defend every inch of allied territory."

Dan convened an emergency meeting of Romania's supreme council of national defence and instructed the foreign ministry to prepare measures regarding the country's relationship with Moscow. Romania's foreign minister, Oana Țoiu, said the government would "officially communicate the consequences that this lack of responsibility on the part of the Russian Federation will have for the diplomatic relations between our countries."

Romanian officials described the incident as a "grave and irresponsible escalation" and a serious breach of international law. Romania's defence ministry said the drone was tracked by radar in Romanian airspace before it crashed. The country requested that NATO accelerate the transfer of anti-drone capabilities and signaled it would invoke Article 4 of the NATO treaty, which triggers formal discussions within the alliance about threats to member security.

Russia denied direct responsibility for the strike. Vladimir Putin claimed without evidence that the drone might have been a stray Ukrainian weapon and suggested the wreckage be handed over to Russia for independent investigation. However, NATO confirmed the drone was "of Russian origin" despite Moscow's denials.

General Gheorghe Maxim, a commander for Romania's armed forces, characterized the strike as not "an attack from Russia against Romania," but emphasized that "Romanians should understand that Russia is a threat to the security of the countries in the area."

The incident drew condemnation from European leaders. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Russia's "war of aggression has crossed yet another line" and pledged solidarity with Romania. France's foreign minister also denounced what he called an "irresponsible act by Russia."

Romania's response reflects broader European concern about the war's potential to expand beyond Ukraine's borders. The strike came amid Russia's intensified campaign of systematic strikes against Ukrainian targets and growing anxiety among NATO members about Russia's hybrid warfare tactics across Eastern Europe.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak overwhelms remote mining town as deaths and infections surge
cards.teaser: Medical workers struggle to contain a surge of Ebola deaths and infections in a remote gold mining town, where the virus spreads with few resources to stop it.
cards.body:
The World Health Organization has estimated the death rate of an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo at between 30% and 50% among confirmed cases. WHO officials describe this mortality rate as "huge," meaning up to five out of every ten people infected are likely to die.

The WHO chief arrived in Congo's capital, Kinshasa, to support containment efforts. WHO leaders have called for a ceasefire among armed groups in the region to help prevent deaths from the disease and aid response operations.

cards.headline: Judge orders Trump's name removed from Kennedy Center
cards.body:
A federal judge has ordered the removal of Donald Trump's name from the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington, ruling that the prestigious venue cannot be renamed without Congressional approval.

U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper issued a 94-page decision on Friday requiring the Trump administration to remove all physical signage bearing Trump's name and eliminate any references to a "Trump Kennedy Center" from official materials within 14 days.

"The Kennedy Center's organic statute makes crystal clear that the Center is to be named for President Kennedy, and it cannot bear any other formal name or public memorial based on the Board's unilateral say-so," Cooper wrote. "Congress gave the Kennedy Center its name, and only Congress can change it."

The judge determined that the Kennedy Center's board of trustees exceeded its authority by unilaterally attempting to rename the institution after Trump. The ruling also temporarily blocked the center from closing this summer for proposed two-year renovations that Trump had announced.

Cooper criticized the board's decision-making process, stating that board members were "derelict in discharging" their responsibilities by basing the closure decision on insufficient information and failing to consider the full consequences for programming and memorial functions. He called the decision to halt operations "ill-informed and seemingly preordained."

The lawsuit was brought by Joyce Beatty, an Ohio Democratic representative who serves on the Kennedy Center's board by virtue of her Congressional position. "Today's ruling rightly affirms that this administration's efforts to rename and close the Center have no basis in law," Beatty said. "The Kennedy Center is an institution that belongs to the American people, not to Donald Trump."

Trump responded to the ruling by posting on Truth Social that he instructed the Department of Commerce to arrange a complete transfer of the Kennedy Center to Congress. "Unless I am free to do what I do better than anyone else, bring this Institution back, physically, financially, and artistically, I have no interest in continuing what could only be a hopeless journey," Trump wrote.

The dispute stems from Trump's appointment of himself as chair of the Kennedy Center's board in February after taking office. He replaced board members with his own appointees, and in December the board voted to add his name to the institution. The move sparked significant controversy, with numerous performing groups and artists canceling bookings in protest, including a run of the Tony Award-winning musical Hamilton. The National Symphony Orchestra's executive director also departed to lead another arts organization.

The Kennedy Center, which receives federal funding, has long been one of America's leading arts venues and enjoyed bipartisan support before becoming embroiled in the Trump administration's broader effort to reshape the nation's cultural institutions.

cards.headline: Four men rescued from flooded Laos cave after 10 days underground
cards.teaser: Two of the seven villagers who entered narrow tunnels searching for gold on May 20 remain missing.
cards.body:
Four men have been rescued from a flooded cave system in Laos after being trapped for 10 days. The villagers, who entered the narrow tunnels on May 20 searching for gold, were freed by divers in a challenging operation.

Of the seven men who initially entered the cave, two remain missing. Rescue teams have faced significant hazards while navigating the flooded tunnels, including muddy water, sharp rocks, and risk of collapse. The first man was rescued on Friday, followed by the four additional rescues.

cards.headline: Exxon warns oil inventories approaching dangerously low levels as Iran conflict blocks trade
cards.body:
Exxon Mobil has warned that global oil inventories are approaching critically low levels within weeks as the conflict with Iran continues to block oil trade routes. The company stated it is nearing inventory levels never previously recorded in the industry.

The ongoing Middle East conflict has strained energy supplies globally, according to warnings from the International Monetary Fund, World Bank, and other international institutions. The situation has created significant pressure on the global oil market.

Exxon indicated the inventory crisis will force oil prices to increase substantially in the near term. Industry analysts have noted the market is facing limited options to address the supply constraints.

One energy analyst characterized the crisis by stating that unlike financial instruments, physical oil supplies cannot be created on demand. The lack of alternative supply routes and the inability to quickly replace blocked shipments has left the market with few tools to manage the shortage.

The Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments, has been affected by the conflict. Concerns are growing about the economic impact on the United States if the strait remains closed or restricted.

Analysts at major financial institutions have warned that the combination of low inventories and continued supply disruptions could push oil prices significantly higher in coming weeks. The situation represents one of the most severe supply crunches in recent years.

The warnings from Exxon and international financial institutions underscore the broader economic risks posed by the continuing conflict. Energy markets have already experienced volatility as traders assess the potential duration of the supply constraints and the likelihood of additional disruptions to oil flows from the region.

cards.headline: Four more men rescued from flooded cave in Laos after 10 days underground
cards.teaser: Rescuers freed four additional men trapped in a flooded cave system in Laos, leaving two villagers still missing after the group entered tunnels searching for gold.
cards.body:
Four miners have been freed from a flooded cave system in Laos following a challenging 10-day rescue operation. The men were part of a group of seven who entered narrow tunnels on May 20 while searching for gold.

Rescue teams navigated hazardous conditions including muddy water, sharp rocks, and narrow passages to extract the trapped miners. Two villagers from the original group remain missing, and divers continue searching through the flooded tunnels to locate them.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak overwhelms remote mining town as deaths and infections surge
cards.teaser: Medical workers struggle to contain a surge of Ebola deaths and infections in a remote gold mining town, where the virus spreads with few resources to stop it.
cards.body:

cards.headline: Colombia votes in presidential election testing strength of Latin American left
cards.teaser: Colombians head to polls as a leftist candidate leads against a far-right rival who calls himself The Tiger in an election seen as crucial for the left in Latin America.
cards.body:
Colombia holds presidential elections on Sunday in a contest between left and right that will shape the country's response to its decades-long armed conflict. The leftist candidate leads in polls but faces a competitive challenge from a far-right outsider.

The election takes place against a backdrop of resurgent political violence. Journalist Mateo Pérez Rueda, a 24-year-old reporting on the conflict between the army, paramilitaries, and dissident groups in Antioquia province, was killed on May 4 while covering the ongoing armed struggle that has defined Colombian politics for decades.

cards.headline: Muslims across Middle East observe Eid amid ongoing conflicts and shortages
cards.teaser: Eid al-Adha celebrations were subdued across the Middle East as war continued and shortages of food and fuel affected the region from Iran to Gaza.
cards.body:
Muslims across the Middle East marked Eid al-Adha with subdued celebrations as conflicts continued throughout the region. From Iran to Gaza, communities struggled with severe shortages of food and fuel that limited traditional holiday observances.

The ongoing wars in multiple areas dampened the festive atmosphere during the religious holiday, preventing many from fully observing the important occasion.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth tells Asian allies to increase contributions for US assistance
cards.teaser: Pete Hegseth outlined how Asian military leaders could prioritize their access to US assistance at a security conference in Singapore.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth addressed Asian military leaders at a security summit in Singapore, outlining how countries could prioritize their access to US assistance. He indicated that greater defense spending commitments from allies would place them ahead in the queue for American support.

At the conference, Hegseth faced questions regarding America's long-term commitment to the region and the status of future arms sales to Asian partners. His remarks emphasized the administration's expectation that allies increase their own defense contributions as part of the US approach to security cooperation in Asia.

cards.headline: Trump meets advisers on Iran deal but no agreement announced
cards.teaser: President Trump held a meeting to make a final determination on Iran negotiations after officials confirmed the US and Iran had agreed on a framework.
cards.body:
President Trump convened with his advisers to make a final decision on Iran negotiations. The meeting followed confirmation from US officials that Washington and Tehran had reached agreement on a deal framework.

No announcement emerged from the session regarding the potential agreement or Trump's determination on how to proceed.

cards.headline: Trump declared fully fit after annual medical examination
cards.teaser: The White House released results from the president's latest checkup showing he is in excellent health.
cards.body:
The White House has released findings from President Trump's annual medical examination. According to his doctor, Trump is in excellent health and fully fit to carry out his presidential duties.

The medical assessment represents the president's latest required health evaluation while in office.

cards.headline: DNA test could help millions of breast cancer patients avoid chemotherapy
cards.teaser: A new international trial shows a screening test may identify which patients can safely skip the treatment.
cards.body:
A groundbreaking genomic test could allow millions of breast cancer patients to skip chemotherapy, according to a new international trial. The test identifies which patients have a low risk of disease recurrence and can be safely treated with hormone therapy alone, achieving near-identical outcomes to chemotherapy-based approaches.

The findings could transform treatment guidelines worldwide. Currently, chemotherapy is routinely recommended after surgery when doctors assess there is a risk the cancer will return. This DNA test offers a way to spare many patients from the side effects of chemotherapy while maintaining treatment effectiveness.

cards.headline: NTSB pulls docket system offline after AI reconstructs cockpit recordings
cards.teaser: The safety board acted after digital images were used to recreate pilot conversations from a recent crash.
cards.body:
The National Transportation Safety Board temporarily shut down its public docket system after artificial intelligence reconstructed cockpit voice recordings from a recent crash. Researchers used digital images available in the NTSB's online docket to recreate audio of pilot conversations.

The agency has long maintained strict confidentiality policies around cockpit audio to protect pilot privacy during investigations. However, advancing AI technology is undermining these privacy protections, forcing the NTSB to reassess how it manages sensitive investigation materials in the digital age.

cards.headline: Texas Senate race focuses on masculinity as Paxton attacks Talarico
cards.teaser: After winning the Republican primary runoff, Ken Paxton called his Democratic opponent too low-T for Texas.
cards.body:
After winning the Republican primary runoff, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton attacked his Democratic opponent, state Representative James Talarico, calling him "too low-T for Texas." The comment put questions about manhood at the center of the Senate race.

The attack highlighted how masculinity has become a defining theme in the matchup between Paxton and Talarico.

cards.headline: Myanmar military leader makes first foreign trip to India
cards.teaser: Min Aung Hlaing's tour comes as Myanmar's government seeks regional support while fighting a civil war.
cards.body:
Myanmar's Min Aung Hlaing made his first foreign tour as leader with a visit to India. The trip is part of the government's effort to strengthen its regional political position.

The visit occurs as Myanmar faces an ongoing civil war. Min Aung Hlaing's administration is working to build international relationships while managing the internal conflict.

cards.headline: Space Force awards SpaceX $4 billion contract for missile-tracking satellite network
cards.teaser: SpaceX received a $4.16 billion contract to build satellites for tracking airborne targets as part of the Golden Dome program.
cards.body:
The U.S. Space Force awarded SpaceX a $4.16 billion contract to develop sensor-equipped satellites for the Golden Dome defense system. These satellites will enable the military to detect and track airborne targets from space, expanding capabilities beyond traditional ground-based radar.

The satellite constellation represents an acceleration of the Space Force's Space Based Airborne Target Indicator Program. The system will provide enhanced monitoring of missiles and other airborne threats, giving the Pentagon real-time tracking capabilities from orbit.

cards.headline: Dell stock hits all-time high as AI demand drives record results
cards.teaser: Dell shares surged to a record high after the company reported strong quarterly results driven by artificial intelligence data center demand.
cards.body:
Dell's stock reached an all-time high following strong quarterly results driven by robust demand for AI infrastructure. The company's servers and storage systems benefited from ongoing investment in AI data centers, leading management to raise its financial forecasts.

The stock surge significantly increased Michael Dell's personal wealth, making him wealthier than Mark Zuckerberg. The strong performance reflects broader momentum in the technology sector, where AI-related chip demand has pushed other companies like SK Hynix and Micron into the trillion-dollar valuation club.

cards.headline: China expands use of digital yuan to lottery draws and government fiscal spending
cards.teaser: China is broadening the applications of its digital currency to include lottery systems and government expenditures.
cards.body:
China has expanded the footprint of its digital yuan by incorporating it into lottery draws and fiscal spending operations. The moves represent an effort to increase adoption of the central bank digital currency beyond consumer transactions.

The expansion comes as China works to establish the digital yuan as a viable alternative in global transactions. Some analysts have suggested that if digital dollar systems become dominant, they could corner global savings, prompting China to accelerate its own digital currency initiatives to maintain financial competitiveness.

cards.headline: Replimune gets third attempt at FDA approval after agency talks
cards.teaser: Replimune will resubmit its cancer drug application after twice being rejected by the FDA, following what the company called productive discussions.
cards.body:
Replimune announced it will make a third attempt to win FDA approval for its cancer drug after holding talks with the agency. The drug had previously been rejected twice by regulators. The announcement came after the departure of FDA official Marty Makary from his position.

Shares of Replimune jumped 80 percent on the news. The company said its recent discussions with the FDA were productive and gave it a pathway to resubmission. The biotech firm is preparing to present new data or information to address the concerns that led to the earlier rejections.

cards.headline: China's rise in drug development prompts concerns about U.S. pharmaceutical dominance
cards.teaser: Clinical trials from China are drawing attention at an international oncology conference as the country's biotechnology sector expands rapidly.
cards.body:
Chinese clinical trials are receiving increased visibility at international oncology conferences, including a recent gathering in Chicago. The country's expanding biotechnology sector is demonstrating growing scientific capacity and substantial investment in pharmaceutical research.

This expansion has sparked concern among U.S. industry observers about potential shifts in global pharmaceutical leadership. China's growing presence in drug development and clinical research is raising questions about the sustainability of American dominance in the biotechnology field.

cards.headline: Wall Street banks navigate risk of missing out on massive SpaceX public offering
cards.teaser: Elon Musk and investment banks are working to convince investors that passing up the SpaceX IPO carries greater risk than participating.
cards.body:
Elon Musk and his bankers are attempting to create momentum around the upcoming SpaceX public offering by framing the decision for investors as one where missing the opportunity poses more risk than buying shares. The strategy aims to build demand for what is expected to be one of the largest initial public offerings in recent years.

For Wall Street firms, the prospect of being excluded from the deal or having clients sit out the offering represents a significant concern. Investment banks are working to position the SpaceX IPO as an opportunity that carries consequences for those who choose not to participate, despite the inherent risks in any large public market debut.

cards.headline: DuckDuckGo search traffic increases following Google AI redesign
cards.teaser: Users have moved to the privacy-focused search engine after Google introduced AI-generated results across its platform.
cards.body:
DuckDuckGo has experienced a surge in installations and search traffic following Google's announcement of an AI-focused redesign of its search engine. The privacy-focused alternative offers users a traditional search experience, contrasting with Google's new AI-generated overviews that appear prominently in results.

Google's shift toward AI summaries prompted some users to explore other search options. DuckDuckGo's conventional search format, which displays traditional website links without AI-generated content, has attracted those seeking alternatives to Google's new direction.

cards.headline: Space Force awards SpaceX $6.45 billion in contracts
cards.teaser: The contracts were announced as SpaceX disclosed that government work accounted for one-fifth of its 2025 revenue.
cards.body:
The US Space Force has awarded SpaceX $6.45 billion in new contracts, the company announced ahead of its initial public offering. The contracts expand SpaceX's existing relationship with the military branch.

SpaceX disclosed in its IPO filing that government contracts account for one-fifth of the company's 2025 revenue, underscoring the significance of its defense and space sector work to its overall business.

cards.headline: Study finds pigeons may navigate using magnetic sensors in their livers
cards.teaser: Researchers have identified a potential mechanism for how the birds detect Earth's magnetic field during flight.
cards.body:
Pigeons may use magnetic sensors located in their livers to navigate, according to a new study. Researchers investigating how the birds orient themselves during flight identified the liver as a possible location for magnetoreception.

The discovery offers an explanation for how pigeons find their way home across long distances, particularly on cloudy days when visual cues are limited. Scientists have long studied how various animals detect magnetic fields, with different species appearing to use different mechanisms for navigation.

cards.headline: Kenyan court blocks US plan to send Ebola-exposed Americans to Kenya
cards.teaser: The Trump administration had proposed relocating exposed individuals to Kenya rather than building specialized facilities.
cards.body:
A Kenyan court has blocked a US government plan to send Americans exposed to Ebola to Kenya for monitoring and treatment. The Trump administration had been building a quarantine and treatment facility in Kenya for Americans who may have been exposed to the virus during the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Some experts have criticized the White House approach, arguing that preventing Americans from returning to the US undermines treatment efforts. The US has previously constructed specialized medical facilities designed to handle Ebola cases and exposures within its own borders.

cards.headline: Nvidia and Microsoft tease new laptop processors ahead of tech conference
cards.teaser: Both companies posted coordinated messages on social media suggesting an announcement about Nvidia's N1X chips.
cards.body:
Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm are coordinating teaser posts on social media ahead of announcements expected this weekend at Computex. The Windows and Nvidia GeForce accounts both posted "A new era of PC," with Arm following suit with similar messaging.

Microsoft's Surface and Windows chief Pavan Davuluri teased new developer-focused hardware coming to the Surface lineup, sharing an image of what appears to be a curved display edge. The coordinated campaign points to upcoming reveals centered on Nvidia's N1X Arm-powered laptop processors.

cards.headline: Researchers warn AI-assisted coding may not improve code quality
cards.teaser: While artificial intelligence helps programmers write code faster, it may not produce better results, according to a new study.
cards.body:
Software developers increasingly rely on artificial intelligence tools to write code, with some refusing to work without AI assistance. Researchers have cautioned that while these tools speed up code production, they may not generate higher-quality software.

The study suggests that faster code production does not necessarily translate to more reliable or maintainable software. Researchers warned that dependency on AI coding tools could create long-term issues for developers and the software they produce.

hero.headline: Djokovic loses French Open match to teenager Fonseca, guaranteeing new Grand Slam champion
hero.body:
Novak Djokovic lost to teenager Joao Fonseca at the French Open, ensuring the tournament will crown a first-time Grand Slam winner. The defeat ended Djokovic's bid for a 25th Grand Slam title.

The loss marks a significant moment in men's tennis. With Djokovic eliminated, the French Open will produce a men's champion who has never won a Grand Slam tournament before. This scenario has not occurred at a Grand Slam event during the Open Era until this year's Roland Garros.

Djokovic, one of the most successful players in tennis history, entered the tournament seeking to add to his record collection of major titles. His elimination opens the draw for players who have yet to capture their first Grand Slam championship.

Fonseca, competing as a teenager, pulled off one of the biggest upsets of the tournament. The Portuguese player's victory over the heavily decorated champion represents a breakthrough performance on one of tennis's biggest stages.

The match took place during the later rounds of the French Open, held at Roland Garros in Paris. Djokovic's absence from the remaining competition creates an opportunity for emerging talent to claim the championship.

Questions about whether age is catching up with Djokovic have intensified following the loss. The Serbian player has dominated men's tennis for more than a decade, winning major titles across all surfaces. His defeat to a much younger opponent has prompted analysis of his current form and future prospects.

The French Open continues with a field that now lacks its most accomplished active player. The remaining competitors will contest for the championship knowing they can become first-time Grand Slam winners.

Djokovic has won the French Open multiple times during his career. This year's early exit prevents him from adding another Roland Garros title to his collection. The tournament will conclude with a new champion being crowned in the men's draw.

cards.headline: Golden Knights to face Hurricanes in Stanley Cup Final starting June 2
cards.teaser: The Vegas Golden Knights will play the Carolina Hurricanes for the Stanley Cup championship.
cards.body:
The Vegas Golden Knights will face the Carolina Hurricanes in the 2026 Stanley Cup Final, with Game 1 scheduled to begin on June 2. The Hurricanes will host the opening games of the series.

The Hurricanes reached their first Stanley Cup Final in 20 years after defeating Montreal in the Eastern Conference Finals. It marks the first time Carolina has advanced to the championship series since 2006, ending a prolonged drought in the postseason under head coach Rod Brind'Amour.

cards.headline: Police arrest fans after brawl before Champions League final in Budapest
cards.teaser: Budapest police made arrests and are reviewing security footage to identify supporters involved in fighting before the Arsenal-Paris St-Germain final.
cards.body:
Police in Budapest have arrested fans and are reviewing CCTV footage following a brawl that broke out before the Champions League final between Arsenal and Paris St-Germain on Saturday. Authorities are using the video evidence to identify additional supporters involved in the violence.

The match took place in the Hungarian capital, which hosted this year's premier European club championship game.

cards.headline: Canada names Alphonso Davies to World Cup squad
cards.teaser: Head coach Jesse Marsch selected Bayern Munich defender Alphonso Davies for what he called the best Canada squad ever assembled.
cards.body:
Head coach Jesse Marsch has selected Bayern Munich defender Alphonso Davies for Canada's World Cup squad this summer. Marsch described the roster as the best Canada squad ever assembled for the tournament.

Davies will be among the key players representing Canada in the competition.

cards.headline: White Sox defeat Tigers 4-3 on Miguel Vargas walk-off home run in 10th inning
cards.teaser: Miguel Vargas hit his first career walk-off home run to give the White Sox a victory after the Tigers bullpen blew multiple leads.
cards.body:
The Chicago White Sox defeated the Detroit Tigers 4-3 in 10 innings, with Miguel Vargas delivering the decisive blow. Vargas hit his first career walk-off home run, igniting celebration at the packed stadium.

The Tigers' bullpen struggled to protect their leads during the contest. Munetaka Murakami exited the game with a hamstring injury before the White Sox mounted their comeback victory.

cards.headline: Giants teammates Abdul Carter and Jaxson Dart address disagreement over Trump rally
cards.teaser: New York Giants players Abdul Carter and Jaxson Dart discussed their differing views after Carter publicly opposed Dart's introduction of Donald Trump at a rally.
cards.body:
Giants defensive player Abdul Carter said he felt compelled to call out teammate Jaxson Dart after the quarterback introduced Donald Trump at a political rally. Carter stated he wanted to make clear he is against Trump.

The two players later expressed unity despite their disagreement. Giants coach John Harbaugh was expected to address the situation at a press conference, though reports indicated he would be unlikely to criticize Dart's appearance at the Trump rally.

cards.headline: Layne Riggs wins NASCAR Truck Series race at Nashville with last-lap pass
cards.teaser: Layne Riggs passed Rajah Caruth on the final lap to win the Truck Series race at Nashville after weather delays.
cards.body:
Layne Riggs won the NASCAR Truck Series race at Nashville Superspeedway. He passed Rajah Caruth in the closing laps to capture the victory in what observers described as a masterclass performance.

The race experienced delays due to inclement weather before resuming. Riggs and Caruth bumped fenders while battling for the win in the final laps before Riggs completed the last-lap pass to take the checkered flag.

hero.headline: Star Wars Editor Marcia Lucas Dies at 80
hero.body:
Marcia Lucas, the Oscar-winning film editor who worked on Star Wars, died at her home in Rancho Mirage, California. She was 80.

Lucas died following a battle with metastatic cancer. Lucasfilm posted a statement expressing the company's sorrow over her death.

She was one of three editors to share an Academy Award for editing the original Star Wars film. Her career included work on several other films from the 1970s, including Taxi Driver.

Lucas was married to Star Wars creator George Lucas. The two later divorced.

Lucasfilm released its tribute statement on Friday, noting the significant role she played in shaping one of cinema's most influential films. Her editing work helped define the pacing and structure of the original Star Wars movie, which premiered in 1977 and became a cultural phenomenon.

Beyond Star Wars, Lucas built a reputation as a skilled editor during a transformative period in American filmmaking. Her work on Taxi Driver, directed by Martin Scorsese and released in 1976, demonstrated her range across different film genres and styles.

The film industry has lost one of its accomplished editors from an era that reshaped Hollywood storytelling. Lucas's contributions to Star Wars remain a fundamental part of the film's enduring legacy, helping to establish the visual and narrative rhythm that would influence science fiction filmmaking for decades to come.

cards.headline: Music Executive Clive Davis Hospitalized in New York
cards.teaser: The 94-year-old music industry veteran was admitted to a New York City hospital with a respiratory issue.
cards.body:
Clive Davis, the music executive who helped shape the careers of numerous artists, was hospitalized in New York City on Friday evening. He was treated for an upper respiratory infection.

Davis is 94 years old. He co-founded Bad Boy Records with Sean Combs and has been a major figure in the music industry for decades. He is expected to recover soon, according to reports.

cards.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Remaining 2026 Tour Dates
cards.teaser: The 92-year-old singer announced he is stepping away from upcoming concerts to focus on his health.
cards.body:
Frankie Valli announced Friday that he is canceling all remaining concert dates for 2026 to focus on his health. The 92-year-old singer shared the news on social media and apologized to fans who purchased tickets.

Despite his age, Valli has maintained an active touring schedule throughout his career and has never lost his passion for performing on the road.

cards.headline: Paul McCartney Reflects on Family Life During Beatles Fame
cards.teaser: The musician discussed how his family helped him navigate life during the Beatles' rise to stardom.
cards.body:
Paul McCartney spoke about a turning point during the Beatles' ascent to fame and how his family helped ground him during that period. The musician detailed how he managed life in the spotlight as Beatlemania swept the world.

McCartney's comments offer insight into the personal challenges faced by members of one of the most famous bands in music history. His family played a key role in helping him maintain perspective during the intense public attention.

cards.headline: Nazanin Zaghari-Ratcliffe Describes Sewing as Lifeline in Iranian Prison
cards.teaser: The former prisoner told an audience that creativity provided a psychological escape during her detention.
cards.body:
Nazanin Zaghari-Ratcliffe spoke about her experience in Iranian prison, describing how sewing became an important outlet during her imprisonment. She addressed an audience about the role of creativity during confinement.

Zaghari-Ratcliffe said that when freedom is restricted, creativity serves as a quick psychological exit. She used sewing as a way to cope with the limitations of detention.

cards.headline: Bill Maher Criticizes Trump's Freedom 250 Concert Series
cards.teaser: The late-night host devoted part of his show to mocking the National Mall concert marking America's 250th birthday.
cards.body:
Bill Maher devoted significant time during his Real Time monologue Friday night to criticizing President Trump's Freedom 250 concert series, scheduled for the National Mall in Washington, D.C. on July 6 to commemorate America's 250th birthday. The event has encountered major obstacles as multiple artists have withdrawn from performing due to political concerns.

The celebration of the nation's anniversary has extended beyond the concert series. The White House is pushing Congress to approve a $250 bill bearing Trump's portrait, according to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. The proposal would require changing federal law that currently prohibits living people from appearing on U.S. currency. Trump allies in Congress are working to create an exception for this commemorative note.

cards.headline: The Killers to Perform at Champions League Final Kickoff
cards.teaser: The rock band will headline the opening show before the match between Arsenal and Paris Saint-Germain.
cards.body:
The Killers will perform at the kickoff show for the Champions League final between Arsenal and PSG on Saturday. The concert is part of the pre-match festivities leading up to the match.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta confirmed that Dutch defender Jurrien Timber is fit to start after recovering from a groin injury that sidelined him for more than two months. Ahead of the final, Arsenal players including Leandro Trossard, Declan Rice, and Eberechi Eze have reflected on what winning the Champions League trophy would mean to them.

hero.headline: US military kills three in latest drug interdiction strike in eastern Pacific
hero.body:
The US military carried out another strike on a boat in the eastern Pacific Ocean on Friday, killing three men in what authorities described as a counter-narcotics operation.

US Southern Command announced the strike, stating that intelligence confirmed the vessel was traveling along known drug-trafficking routes and engaged in narco-trafficking operations. The command said the boat was operated by designated terrorist organizations, though it provided no evidence to support these claims.

A 16-second video posted by Southern Command shows a single strike being launched at the boat, which subsequently burst into flames. No US military forces were harmed in the operation.

The Friday strike marks the third attack this week and brings the total number of people killed in US military strikes on suspected drug-smuggling boats since September to at least 148. An earlier strike earlier in the week killed 11 people, making it one of the deadliest attacks this year.

The operations are part of the Trump administration's expanded military campaign in the region to intercept alleged drug traffickers. US Southern Command, which oversees military operations in Latin America and the Caribbean, is now led by General Francis Donovan.

However, the legality of these strikes has drawn increasing scrutiny from lawmakers and legal experts. Some have raised concerns that the Pentagon is conducting extrajudicial killings and exercising what they characterize as "abuse of power with life-or-death consequences."

According to a statement from the American Civil Liberties Union, "Under both U.S. and international law, it is flagrantly illegal to use the military to kill civilians suspected only of crimes. Civilians, including those suspected of smuggling drugs, are not lawful targets."

The ACLU statement continued: "Just because the Trump administration says these strikes are firmly grounded in law doesn't make it true."

General Donovan took over leadership of US Southern Command following the abrupt retirement of Admiral Alvin Holsey, who reportedly left over disagreements concerning the strike policy.

The eastern Pacific has long served as a major transit route for cocaine and other narcotics moving from South American production areas toward Central America and Mexico. Drug trafficking organizations have increasingly turned to small boats and semi-submersible vessels to move cargo through the region.

The US military has expanded its role in counter-narcotics operations in recent years, working with the Coast Guard and partner nations to intercept suspected trafficking vessels. These operations have sometimes involved the use of force when boats fail to stop or are deemed to pose a threat.

Southern Command did not provide additional operational details about Friday's engagement, including when precisely the strike occurred.

cards.headline: Trump administration shifts Ebola response to border controls as outbreak grows
cards.teaser: The Trump administration has adopted increasingly isolationist policies in response to the Ebola outbreak in Congo and Uganda, focusing on keeping the disease out of the US.
cards.body:
The World Health Organization reports that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 1,000 suspected cases with a death rate between 30% and 50%. The WHO chief traveled to Congo's capital to support containment efforts and called for ceasefires among armed groups to prevent additional deaths from the preventable disease.

The Trump administration has prioritized border security and isolation measures in response to the outbreak, drawing criticism from infectious disease experts who favor more robust international engagement in fighting the disease abroad.

cards.headline: Trump physician releases memo saying president in excellent health after checkup
cards.teaser: President Trump remains in excellent health, his physician wrote in a memo following the president's annual physical exam at Walter Reed.
cards.body:
President Trump's physician released a memo stating the president is in "excellent health" and "fully fit" to carry out his duties following his annual physical exam at Walter Reed National Military Medical Center earlier this week.

However, independent physicians have raised questions about recurrent bruises on his hands and swelling in his legs, according to the medical report.

cards.headline: Trump plans UFC fight on White House lawn as part of America 250 celebrations
cards.teaser: President Trump is hosting a UFC fight on the White House lawn next month and has pushed to put his face on a $250 bill.
cards.body:
The White House is staging a UFC prime-time fight next month as part of the America 250 celebrations. President Trump is expected to attend the event, which has been in preparation for weeks.

The Trump administration is also pursuing a $250 bill bearing the president's portrait to commemorate the country's 250th anniversary of independence. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced the White House is pushing Congress to approve the measure, which would require changing federal law that currently prohibits living people from appearing on US currency. The treasury has already begun preparing for the possibility of the new banknote, though Democrats have vowed to block the move.

cards.headline: Former Border Patrol commander urges ICE agents to 'give them hell' after New Jersey clashes
cards.teaser: Greg Bovino issued a message of support to immigration agents amid clashes between federal officers and protesters outside a New Jersey detention center.
cards.body:
Former US Border Patrol commander-at-large Greg Bovino posted a message of support to Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents following clashes between federal officers and protesters outside Delaney Hall immigration detention center in New Jersey. Bovino urged the agents to "give them hell" in his statement.

The tensions at the facility prompted action from New Jersey state officials. Governor Mikie Sherrill and Attorney General Jennifer Davenport announced that state police would take over policing functions from federal immigration officers outside the center. As part of the transition, state police will establish a designated "peaceful protected zone" for demonstrators.

cards.headline: Manhood becomes central theme in Texas Senate race between Paxton and Talarico
cards.teaser: Ken Paxton attacked Democratic nominee James Talarico as too low-T for Texas after winning the Republican primary runoff.
cards.body:
Ken Paxton launched his general election campaign against Democratic state Rep. James Talarico by questioning the opponent's masculinity, calling him "too low-T for Texas" immediately after winning the Republican primary runoff.

The attack signals that gender and masculinity will play a significant role in the upcoming Senate race between the two candidates.

cards.headline: Lawmakers criticize single-party primaries for limiting voter choice
cards.teaser: Some lawmakers say closed, single-party primaries limit voter choice and incentivize officials to prioritize party loyalty over broader representation.
cards.body:
Some lawmakers are criticizing closed, single-party primaries, arguing that the system restricts voter choice and pushes elected officials to prioritize loyalty to their party over broader interests.

These primary elections shape how members of Congress behave once in office. The structure creates incentives for politicians to appeal primarily to party base voters rather than reaching out to wider constituencies, according to the critics.
